data.name: Jogesh
data.long_meaning: The name Jogesh is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Jagat' which means 'world' and 'Ish' which means 'lord'. The name Jogesh signifies the one who is the lord of the earth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jogesh is of Hindu origin and holds a significant cultural impact for Hindus as it symbolizes power and control over the material world. It is a name often given to boys who are expected to grow up to be strong and influential figures in their community.
data.spiritual_significance: Jogesh represents the divine presence of God on earth. The name signifies that the individual bearing the name is a representative of the divine and is responsible for upholding spiritual values and maintaining harmony in the world around them.

historical_references.reference: Jogesh Chandra Chatterji was a noted Indian historian, born on 24 June 1897 in Kolkata, British India. He was the first professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta.
Jogesh Mukherjee was a Shankaracharya of the Advaita order of Hindu monasticism, born on 11 September 1915. He was the head of the Shankaracharya lineage at Puri, Odisha, from 1967 to 1994.
